title: Predictive-step autoscaler with safety windows and tokenized throughput guarantees
creator: Maya Patel
description: Design and implement a new autoscaling policy engine variant for Dedicated fleets that combines short-term demand forecasting with discrete step scaling and explicit per-tenant throughput guarantees. The policy should: (1) provide firm tokenized throughput guarantees for contracted tenants; (2) reduce oscillation and unnecessary churn using safety windows (temporal hysteresis) and scheduled attenuation; (3) allow cost-aware step decisions with explicit rollback criteria; (4) interoperate with routing/fallback so that when Dedicated capacity is constrained traffic can failover to compatible hosted or lower-tier model variants.
design_notes: Core idea is a predictive-step controller: use a lightweight 1-minute quantile forecaster (P95 demand over next 2 minutes) and map forecasted need to discrete scale steps (eg. +1 GPU, +2 GPUs) with an additive safety window. We introduce a tokenized guarantee ledger per tenant where each guaranteed throughput purchase mints 'tokens' representing steady-state request-per-second credit. When tokens are low, scaler prioritizes capacity for guarantee-bearing tenants and activates a burst-lease mechanism that decays over a configurable window. Safety windows are two-fold: a warm safety window (short, e.g., 90s) where scale-ups are allowed aggressively, and a persistent safety fence (longer, e.g., 20m) that prevents rapid scale-downs. All scale actions must record rationale metadata to the audit log for later analysis. The policy runs in the scaling controller and exposes tunables: forecast_quantile, step_map, warm_window_s, persist_fence_m, burst_lease_decay_s, tenant_token_threshold.
algorithm_summary: 1) aggregate per-fleet effective RPS and per-tenant guaranteed RPS tokens. 2) compute 1-minute sliding forecasts for P50/P95. 3) compute desired headroom = max(forecasted_demand + safety_margin, guaranteed_token_demand). 4) map desired headroom to discrete steps via step_map and cost_penalty. 5) apply safety windows and opaque cooldowns; if within warm window allow step; if within persistent fence block scale-downs. 6) when capacity lacking, activate burst-lease for guarantee-tenants and trigger spillover routing policy. 7) emit events to console and ledger updates.
acceptance_criteria: Policy can enforce per-tenant guaranteed throughput under normal load 99% of the time in test harness (SLO: 99th percentile guarantee compliance)
Predictive-step scaling reduces unnecessary scale events vs baseline PID scaler by >= 30% in replayed production traces
Safety windows prevent oscillatory scale-downs: no more than one scale-down within persistent_fence_m for stable workloads
Burst-lease mechanism honors decay schedule and does not permanently starve non-guaranteed tenants
All scale decisions are auditable with a human-readable rationale attached to the scaling event
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable policy in a single non-customer-critical fleet for 72 hours with verbose logging
Phase 2 (pilot): enable for 5 medium-sized dedicated fleets (mixed tenants) and monitor guarantee compliance and cost delta for 7 days
Phase 3 (gradual): roll out to all new Dedicated deployments behind a feature flag and allow opt-in for existing customers
Fallback: revert to existing proportional headroom autoscaler and trigger incident runbook if guarantees not met
test_plan: Unit tests for mapping table (step_map) and token ledger operations
Replay-driven integration tests using 30-day production trace: measure scale event counts, guarantee compliance, and cost overhead
Chaos tests: simulate delayed GPU provisioning and validate spillover routing and lease decay behavior
End-to-end smoke with staging: tenant purchase of tokens leads to expected prioritization under constrained capacity
monitoring: Console dashboard: per-fleet scale actions, forecast vs actual demand, guarantee compliance rate
SLO alerts: guarantee_violation_rate > 0.5% within 5m -> P0 alert
Cost dashboard: additional GPU-hours attributable to policy vs baseline
Audit stream: scaling_decision events indexed by tenant and fleet
implementation_notes: Implementation will extend the scaling controller to ingest token ledger via existing tenant metadata API. Forecasting component should be implemented as a small stateless service using exponentially-weighted percentiles for stability. Step_map is a configurable policy object (CSV-like string in config). Ensure idempotent scale actions using controller action IDs. Add feature flag and per-fleet toggles. Limit memory/CPU overhead of forecasting to < 1% of controller resources.
risks_and_mitigation: Forecast errors can cause over-provisioning: mitigate via conservative forecast_quantile and cost_penalty parameter that biases towards smaller steps
Token ledger inconsistency: use lease-backed updates with reconciliation job; expose manual override for SRE
Tenant fairness concerns: implement max-burst-per-window and proportional drain for non-guaranteed traffic
Scale latency when underlying infra provisioning is slow: integrate with warm-lanes/standby pools for fast headroom allocations
